summary.motive: Destroy Two-High Quarters coverage by crossing the release paths of the #1 and #2 receivers on deep vertical tracks, triggering coverage miscommunication and blown assignments.
summary.whyItWorks: In Quarters coverage, DBs play pattern-match rules based on receiver releases. When the outside receiver breaks inside on a post and the slot receiver wheels outside, both DBs frequently bite on the inside post, leaving the wheel vertical completely unguarded.
summary.failureMode: A safety and corner who execute seamless "switch" communication, or a 4-man defensive pass rush that gets home before the 5-step deep route develops.

beats.title: Spread 11-Personnel Quarters Attack
beats.text: Steichen dials up a deep 4-verticals switch concept against Two-High Quarters coverage, targeting the spatial rules of the field safety and cornerback.

beats.title: The 6-Yard Stem Switch Confusion
beats.text: Slot H stems inside while outside Z crosses over the top. At 6 yards, they swap vertical tracks, causing instant panic between RCB and Strong Safety SS.

beats.title: Double-Coverage on Post Leaves Sideline Naked
beats.text: Both RCB and SS squeeze inside to match Z on the post, leaving slot receiver H blowing completely uncontested down the wide open right sideline.

beats.title: The 35-Yard Touchdown Bomb
beats.text: QB steps cleanly into the pocket and delivers a breathtaking 35-yard dime to H in stride for an explosive touchdown.

relations.tell: Slot H and outside Z cross stems at 6 yards on vertical release instead of standard screen/blocking releases.
